title: Why Do Fighter Jets Look So Weird?
description:
Some of the most advanced fighter jets in the world are designed to be unstable. Without a computer correcting them many times every second, they would flip out of control. Their tails lean sideways, their doors have teeth, their pilots lie almost on their backs, and some of them have a strange bump right in front of the engine. It all looks wrong. Today, ten fighter jet parts that look wrong, and why every one of them is right.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:18 1. The little front wings
3:17 2. The wing extensions
4:51 3. The tails that lean
6:18 4. The teeth on the doors
7:48 5. The gold canopy
9:18 6. The bump in front of the engine
10:43 7. The nozzles that move
12:07 8. The seat that leans back
13:39 9. The yellow handle
15:07 10. The hook on the tail
16:31 The verdict

Sources:
- F-16 relaxed static stability, fly-by-wire, side-stick, 30-degree seat, bubble canopy: Wikipedia, "General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon
- Canards and unstable delta designs: Wikipedia, "Canard (aeronautics)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canard_(aeronautics) ; "Eurofighter Typhoon" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurofighter_Typhoon
- Leading edge extensions and vortex lift: Wikipedia, "Leading-edge extension" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leading-edge_extension
- Stealth shaping, edge alignment, sawtooth panels, internal weapons: Wikipedia, "Stealth technology" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stealth_technology
- Diverterless supersonic inlet (Lockheed, first flight 11 Dec 1996 on an F-16, ~30% lighter): Wikipedia, "Diverterless supersonic inlet" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diverterless_supersonic_inlet
- F119 two-dimensional nozzle, 20 degrees up or down: Pratt & Whitney (RTX), "F119 Engine" https://www.rtx.com/en/prattwhitney/products/military-engines/f119
- Martin-Baker lives saved (7,827 as of Aug 2026), zero-zero seats: EurAsian Times https://www.eurasiantimes.com/f-35-saab-gripen-jet-crashes-martin-baker-seats-save-two-more-pilots-total-now-at-7827/
- Carrier arresting gear and bolters: Wikipedia, "Arresting gear" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arresting_gear
